lines.say: At dynamic equilibrium, forward and reverse rates are equal. Concentrations stay constant.
K is products over reactants, each raised to its coefficient.
Leave out pure solids, pure liquids and solvent water. Their activity is 1.
Big K means products dominate. Small K means reactants dominate.
K only depends on temperature.
Reverse the reaction, and K becomes one over K.
Multiply the coefficients by n, and K becomes K to the n.
Add two reactions, and multiply their K values.
For gases, K p equals K c times R T to the delta n.
For N 2 O 4 going to 2 N O 2, delta n is plus 1.
Multiply K c, 4.6 times 10 to the minus 3, by R T, 24.78.
So K p is about 0.11. Only gases count in delta n.
Q has the same form as K, but uses concentrations right now.
Q less than K: too few products. The reaction goes forward.

draw.alt: Q below K, arrow pointing forward

lines.say: Q greater than K: too many products. It goes in reverse.
Q equals K: it's at equilibrium.
Initial, Change, Equilibrium. Let x be the change, using the stoichiometry.
H 2 starts at 0.200, I 2 at 0.100. They lose x each. H I gains 2 x.
K is 50, so this gives a quadratic. The roots are 0.0934 and 0.233.
0.233 would make iodine negative. Reject it.

draw.alt: Two roots, the larger one rejected

lines.say: So H I is 0.187 molar at equilibrium.
If K is tiny, use the small x shortcut. Then check x is under 5 percent.
Disturb an equilibrium, and it shifts to partly undo the change.
Add a reactant: Q drops below K, so it shifts forward. K doesn't change.
Squeeze the volume: it shifts to the side with fewer gas moles.

draw.alt: Smaller container shifts to side with fewer gas particles

lines.say: Adding inert gas at constant volume changes nothing.
Temperature changes K itself. Heat an exothermic reaction, and K falls.
A catalyst gets there faster, but doesn't move the position.
Delta G nought equals minus R T ln K.
Negative delta G nought means K is bigger than 1.
For ammonia, delta G nought is minus 32.9 kilojoules. Convert to joules first.
ln K is 13.28. So K is about 5.8 times 10 to the 5.
Use R 0.08314 for K p. Use 8.314 for delta G.
Only gases count in delta n.
Pressure and concentration don't change K. Only temperature does.
Never keep a root that gives a negative concentration.
